inspiration.observed_pattern: A MariaDB regression query self-joins one table, groups by a column from the left alias, and applies ordered GROUP_CONCAT to the grouped values.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an organizational reporting query. A member table self-joins managers to their direct reports, and each manager's report names are ordered within GROUP_CONCAT using a fixed separator; all schema, identifiers, values, and business context are new.

fixture_notes: Manager 100 has reports 101 and 102, whose names must be alphabetized inside one pipe-delimited GROUP_CONCAT value. Manager 200 has one report; member 300 has no manager and must be absent from the self-join result.
determinism_notes: Fixed member IDs, manager links, explicit report-name ordering, fixed GROUP_CONCAT separator, and final manager ordering are used; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE org_members (member_id INT PRIMARY KEY, member_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, manager_id INT NULL)
INSERT INTO org_members VALUES (100, 'Mira', NULL), (101, 'Zane', 100), (102, 'Asha', 100), (200, 'Noel', NULL), (201, 'Iris', 200), (300, 'Solo', NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT manager.member_id, manager.member_name, GROUP_CONCAT(report.member_name ORDER BY report.member_name ASC SEPARATOR '|') AS direct_reports FROM org_members AS manager INNER JOIN org_members AS report ON report.manager_id = manager.member_id GROUP BY manager.member_id, manager.member_name ORDER BY manager.member_id
SELECT member_id, member_name, manager_id FROM org_members ORDER BY member_id
